chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not leave for people in their religion any proof except through Imams from among them, whom He commanded them to obey and forbade them from disobeying.
ai.seo_question: What is the divine proof (hujjah) for people in their religion according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishing the Imams as the definitive divine proofs (hujjah) for humanity, emphasizing their infallibility and the obligatory nature of their obedience. This narration underscores the Shia doctrine of *Nass* (divine designation), positioning the Imams not merely as scholars but as the essential link between the divine law and the community, ensuring the preservation of religious truth after the Prophet.
